title: Lesson 2.1 Knowledge Check
description: Five questions on prompting and directing a text model for dramatic writing. Unlimited attempts; your best score counts.

questions.text: Which elements belong in a scene brief? Select all that apply.
questions.feedback: The six elements are characters, objective, obstacle, setting, tone, and form.

questions.text: Which is the most effective director's note for a revision round?
options: Cut the first six lines and start with her already holding the trumpet case
questions.feedback: Specific, actionable notes produce specific rewrites. Vague notes produce vague ones.

questions.text: A text model's first-draft scene is usually finished and ready for a table read.
questions.feedback: First drafts are competent and forgettable. Directed revision and a human rewrite make the scene yours.

questions.text: Models tend to write characters who say exactly what they feel. The human rewrite fixes this mainly by adding:
options: Subtext, deflection, and things left unsaid
questions.feedback: Real dialogue works through subtext. Cutting explanation and adding what is unsaid is the core of the rewrite.

questions.text: What minimum share of the dialogue does this lesson ask you to rewrite yourself?
options: None; the model's revision is enough
questions.feedback: At least a third, marked so a reader can see what you changed.
